title: Audit and consolidate CI pipelines; migrate to hermetic builds and remote cache
creator: Carlos Mendes
description: Summary: Consolidate disparate GitHub Actions workflows and legacy Jenkins jobs into a small number of hermetic, cache-friendly pipelines. Deliver reproducible build artifacts, faster feedback loops for engineers, and reduced CI cost by enabling remote build caching and improved image layering. Background: Over several years we've accumulated per-repo divergent CI configs, multiple base images, and ad-hoc caching. This has led to slow onboarding, flaky builds, and expensive repeated downloads. Goals: 1) Audit all active CI pipelines and identify common stages; 2) Standardize on BuildKit-based Dockerfiles and a pinned minimal base image catalog; 3) Enable remote caching (S3/GCS-backed BuildKit cache + action-cache) and warm caches for important branches; 4) Upgrade linters/toolchains (golangci-lint, ESLint, Prettier, Python black) and pin runtime toolchains for hermetic builds; 5) Reduce general job runtime by 30% on average and cut redundant image layers; 6) Provide a migration guide and a scriptable upgrade path for repo owners.
tasks: Inventory: run script to enumerate workflows, images, and cache usage across org (script: tools/ci-inventory.sh)
Design: create standardized CI manifest templates (node, go, python, infra) and publish to infra repo
Dockerfiles: convert top 25 repos to multi-stage BuildKit-optimized images (distroless where possible), add --platform support
Caching: configure remote BuildKit cache backed by GCS with signed URLs and action cache fallback
Tooling: upgrade golangci-lint to v1.60, eslint to 8.x, node from 18 -> 20 in runner images, pin Python to 3.11
Workflows: replace duplicate workflows with reusable composite actions and centralize secrets access via org-level secrets
QA: add smoke job that verifies artifact checksum parity after migration
Docs: publish migration guide and checklist, create 1:1 office hours for early movers
Rollout: pilot on repo A, then batch-migrate 10 repos/week using automation script
Metrics: add dashboard (Grafana) to track median job time, cache hit rate, and bandwidth savings
acceptance_criteria: Top 10 busiest repos migrated with >75% cache hit rate on main branches
Median build time across migrated repos reduced by at least 25%
All migrated pipelines produce reproducible artifact checksums between local BuildKit and CI
Linters/tools pinned and run in hermetic containers, no more network fetching at runtime
Migration guide and runbook published and referenced in at least three PRs
No customer-facing regressions and post-migration alerts remain at low severity for two weeks
recent_updates: 2025-02-18: Inventory script run across 142 repos; initial spreadsheet created (links below). Observed 7 distinct base image families and 3 different golangci-lint versions.
2025-02-22: Decided to standardize on BuildKit with remote cache on GCS. Trade-off: added infra cost vs. large cache savings; chosen because bandwidth outweighs storage cost.

2025-02-25: PR created to add shared ci-templates repo and composite actions (https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-templates/pull/12). Feedback from infra-team: prefer org-level secrets to reduce per-repo setup.
2025-02-27: Pilot conversion completed for repo infra-agent. Build time down 37%, cache hit rate 82% after warmup. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-agent/pull/3421
2025-03-03: Started coordinating rollout with platform ownership; created schedule and auto-migration script (tools/ci-migrate.py).
review_comments: PM (Jen Lo): Please surface cost delta estimates in the proposal; include worst-case egress costs for GCS.
Security (Marta Ruiz): Ensure GCS cache credentials use short-lived tokens and KMS-wrapped keys; avoid long-lived service account keys in repos.
Eng Lead (Ravi Iyer): Suggest we add a fallback path to action cache for repos with restricted network egress.
QA (Leah Kim): Add deterministic snapshot tests to verify produced artifacts across builders.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cache poisoning or inconsistent cache entries. Mitigation: Use content-addressable keys + builder metadata and snapshot checksums; invalidate caches on major tool upgrades.
Risk: Build failures after tool upgrades (linters/runtimes). Mitigation: Run dry-run upgrades in parallel CI and provide automatic revertable PRs.
Risk: Secrets exposure when centralizing. Mitigation: Use org-level secrets and short-lived tokens; restrict who can edit composite actions.
Risk: Cost spike from initial cache warm-up. Mitigation: Warm caches during off-peak hours and stagger repo migrations; monitor and cap network egress.
qa_notes: Add job that runs 'ci-verify' which compares artifact checksums against a canonical build produced in a controlled environment.
Add lint gating to prevent merged PRs that revert pinned tool versions.
Include a rollback Playbook that reverts to previous workflow file and clears cache keys for problematic migrations.
